title: Come back when you are taller
idea: A height mark on a doorframe means nothing until there is a second one above it. The page is the edge of a doorframe with one pencil mark already on it, dated the day the site began; hold still against the paint and a mark is pencilled for you with today's date, and the frame keeps it, so the piece only finishes when you return. The room beyond the door is as light or dark as your own hour.

title: Under the paint
idea: Nobody rubs out a height mark; they paint over it, so every one ever made is still on the frame, sealed between two coats. The page is the jamb from 0 seen close, and scrolling sands it back through ninety-five years of colours in widening rings, each coat giving up the initials and dates pencilled on it just before the same sanding takes them off. It ends at bare pine and the carpenter's figure for the door, and scrolling back up does not put anything back.
